answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to build a bridge of verifiable work before it can trade: an agent earns trust by completing small, publicly checkable tasks over time, like a reef growing coral by coral, rather than arriving fully formed. A newcomer that flashes past like a comet, with no history and no stake, cannot flood the market with copies, because every copy must repeat the same slow, costly climb. Cheap identities stay light; earned reputation carries weight.
